newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKIA "UNDERSTANDS" U.S. BOMBING OF IRAQ.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKIA "UNDERSTANDS" U.S. BOMBING OF IRAQ.

text.p: Slovakia views the recent United States bombing raids on Iraq "with understanding", but withholds comment on Washington's methods, the country's newly-installed Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik said on Thursday.

Speaking in his first news conference since his appointment as minister a week ago, Hamzik said Slovakia had expressed its basic attitude towards Iraq by participating in the U.S.-led "Operation Desert Storm" military intervention in 1991.
"We took part in Desert Storm which was an unequivocal expression of our basic stance," he said. "We view the latest U.S. moves with understanding, though we do not wish to comment the methods."
After Iraqi military moves in the Kurdish north, the U.S. fired a total of 44 cruise missiles on Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday.
The missles were aimed at air defence targets in southern Iraq to minimise Iraqi resistance to U.S. warplanes policing an expanded no-fly zone.

Slovak troops took part in Desert Storm which forced Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1991 as part of a then Czechoslovak contingent. The country split into the Czech and Slovak Republics in January 1993.
Slovakia, like the Czech Republic, has made membership in NATO and the European Union a focus of its foreign policy.
Hamzik, who before his appointment in a cabinet reshuffle last week was ambassador to Bonn, said under his tenure Slovakia's foreign political priorities would not change.
"We remain on course in our committments to integration in Altantic and European structures," Hamzik said.
The new minister has scheduled visits later this month to Washington, Moscow. Kiev, Prague and Budapest.
He has already met his German and Austrian counterparts Klaus Kinkel and Wolfgang Schuessel.
